priorities.name: Quiet, private space for focused and customer-facing work
priorities.issue: Associates in focus- and call-heavy roles can't consistently get a quiet, private workspace, and comments tie this directly to needing to work from home to do the job.
whatItLooksLike: I am in customer service role so I need to be in an environment that is quiet and job does not support it need to be at home like I was for the past 9 years
The inability to consistently have a private work space with multiple screens as I have in my home office.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (75/100); focused-work friction 29/100 (60% under-supported).
Noise & Distraction: 27 comments (59% neg); Privacy & Confidentiality: 32 comments (47% neg).
Work Activity is the site's weakest dimension (60.5, rank 8) despite strong Service and Physical scores.

priorities.proposedAction: Map which roles need sustained quiet/private space and match them to quiet neighborhoods or bookable enclosed space; validate capacity before build-out.
priorities.siteMustDo: Identify the affected teams, trial a quiet neighborhood, and size any enclosed-space gap for Workplace Solutions.

priorities.name: Desk reservation model and dual-monitor setup
priorities.issue: Daily reserve-and-reset is seen as cumbersome, and 'dual' monitors are wired to mirror rather than extend, so associates don't get the setup they expect.
whatItLooksLike: Would prefer a permanent seat in the PulsePoint with a 3+ days in the office requirement. Reserving my workspace and resetting my workspace every day is cumbersome
At our Pulse Point, the dual monitors are plugged into each other so you don't get the value of dual  you just get two versions of the same thing.

evidence.text: Desk Availability & Reservations: 45 comments, 60% negative (cited at 30% of comments vs. 28% company).
Hardware: 39 comments, 49% negative — the mirrored dual-monitor issue is a concrete, fixable defect.

priorities.proposedAction: Fix the dual-monitor extend/mirror configuration as an immediate technical correction, and review whether high-attendance teams warrant assigned/neighborhood seating.
priorities.siteMustDo: Correct the monitor configuration site-wide now; separately assess a seating model for 3+-day teams.

priorities.name: Thermal comfort (temperature)
priorities.issue: Temperature runs too cold and is among the most negative specific complaints.
whatItLooksLike: People should be cognizant of others on conference calls. Temperature is way too cold.

evidence.text: Temperature / Thermal: 17 comments, 82% negative — the most-negative theme at the site.

priorities.proposedAction: Facilities to check set-points/balancing in the cold zones and confirm the fix.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log cold zones/times, submit to building ops, and verify the correction.

priorities.name: Virtual-meeting readiness: webcams and room screen-sharing
priorities.issue: Hybrid meetings are harder than they should be: many desks and focus cubes lack a webcam, and conference-room screen-sharing doesn't work reliably.
whatItLooksLike: …Most cubes lack a webcam, which means you have you use the blurry laptop camera
Conference room share screen features don't work properly. …

evidence.text: Virtual collaboration with remote/hybrid colleagues: Under Supported — friction 26/100 (51% under-supported), the highest-friction item at the site after the focus and discretion items covered by P1.
AV / Video Conferencing: 11 comments, 73% negative; Meeting & Conference Rooms: 12 comments, 75% negative.
Video conferencing & meeting-room technology agreement: 3.75 vs 3.72 company average (Moderate).
P1 covers call privacy and P2 covers monitors; this priority is the camera and room screen-share gap.

priorities.proposedAction: Have Technology test screen-sharing in every conference room and fix failures, and confirm webcam coverage at workstations and focus cubes — adding cameras where desks are used for video calls.
priorities.siteMustDo: Run a room-by-room screen-share test with Technology, count workstations without a camera, and confirm the fixes within 30 days.

priorities.name: Food options without leaving the tower
priorities.issue: On-site food and snack options are limited and pricey, and the nearest meal means a long elevator trip down and back.
whatItLooksLike: Meal Options for purchase. Willis Tower has many options on the main level, but it would take 10 minute elevator ride each way (down and up) plus the wait for the food (busy area)
More affordable food options available on site
Better snack and beverage options, which unfortunately would probably be less healthy than the current options. …

evidence.text: Availability of on-site food and beverage options: Under Supported — friction 17/100 (35% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Review the pantry/market range and pricing with Food & Beverage, and test a pre-order or delivery option with the building's main-level vendors.
priorities.siteMustDo: Pulse-check which items and price points associates want, pilot one change for 30 days, and measure uptake.

protectWhatIsWorking.evidence: 81/100, rank 2 — a strength (food & beverage availability is the exception — see priority 5)
protectWhatIsWorking.note: Maintain the current service level and monitor performance.
Maintain the current service level and monitor performance.

assumptions: The mirrored dual-monitor issue is treated as a real defect based on comments; confirm onsite it's configuration, not per-desk hardware.
